lg.gloss.pass_price.dd: The share price at which the Buffett Zone opens. The arithmetic is this site's; the attitude comes from the 1997 shareholder letter — for anyone who will keep adding shares in the years ahead, a falling price is not a loss but a sale. It's the line about whether someone who will eat hamburgers all their life should welcome or regret a drop in beef prices. So this column is not a forecast; it is where we write down, in advance, the price tag we are waiting for. It is arithmetic on today's ruler (the g assumption), so if the assumption changes, so does this price.
lg.gloss.pik.dd: Being paid rent in IOUs instead of cash. If profit shows up on the books but goes back into construction before it reaches shareholders, all the owner holds is paper. This badge goes on buildings whose conversion rate (what reaches shareholders ÷ book profit) is negative.
lg.gloss.title: Glossary — how to read this table's ruler
lg.gloss.too_hard.dd: A building whose rent column 10 years out is blank. Not because it is a bad building, but because nobody can fill that column with confidence — in his 2000 letter Buffett said committing capital in such cases should be called speculation. A machine never assigns this badge. It goes only on buildings where a human wrote "business certainty ✕" in the judgment layer.
lg.gloss.zone.dd: Does this building's rent beat Treasury interest? (The 3x and 1.5x thresholds are our own.) If the cost coupon 10 years out exceeds 3x the Treasury yield it is a Pass; at 1.5–3x it Needs Proof of Growth (today's price isn't enough — growth has to actually arrive); below 1.5x it is Bond-Inferior — taking on risk and still doing worse than Treasuries. Buildings whose research isn't finished, so the math can't be done, are Untested. Untested is not bad — it is blank.

lg.notice_html: The Buffett Zone is the arithmetic result of plugging today's price into a standard of our own, in which UNIVERTRIX turned ideas from Buffett's letters (1992 · 2000) into a ruler (the 3x and 1.5x thresholds are not Buffett's numbers but values set by this site), and it is not investment advice. The g in the 10-year cost coupon is an assumption. If the assumption changes, so does the conclusion — which is why every coupon in the table sits next to its assumption. Auto-researched values are based on filings and AI extraction and may contain errors — those are the values marked 'Auto'. The pass price is arithmetic on the current ruler (the g assumption), not a price target. Nothing here is a buy or sell signal.
lg.roe.norate: Bond yield not wired · tangible ROE {r}
lg.tip.arith: Business certainty ✕ — a pass on arithmetic only; by Buffett's standard it is too hard to estimate (2000 letter)
lg.tip.auto: Machine-filled value — extracted from filings (SEC XBRL) or AI research. The mark disappears once a human researches and overwrites it.
lg.tip.cap: The assumed growth rate is pinned at the {g} cap
lg.tip.hard: A building whose rent column 10 years out cannot be filled with confidence (business certainty ✕). Not a failing grade but the honesty of "we don't know" — a human wrote it that way in the judgment layer.
lg.tip.peak: A warning light for cyclicals only. A coupon computed on peak earnings is a ceiling that looks like a floor — so the coupon is shown for reference only, with no zone call and no pass price.
lg.tip.pik: Like being paid interest in paper (reinvestment) instead of cash. A negative conversion rate means book profit went back into construction before reaching shareholders.
lg.tip.unadj: Foreign filings used without adjustment — based on accounting profit that still includes investment gains and losses.
lg.tip.weak: An assumption built on forecasts alone — not cross-checked against historical growth. A number came out, but there is no track record behind it.

px.gloss.cyclical.dd: A building whose rent is set by the weather (the economy), not the owner (memory · banks · energy). Rent goes up 3 times in a boom; in a bust, it stands empty. So the gap is shown, but no zone is assigned.
px.gloss.flight.dd: The rent comes in nicely, but raising it means calling in the cranes every time (TSMC · Lilly). High quality, yet much of what it earns goes straight back into construction.
px.gloss.float.dd: An owner who earns not from rent but by investing tenants' deposits for free (Berkshire). On the rent ledger (P/E) alone it looks cheap forever, so this parallax gauge does not measure it.
px.gloss.peak_tail: That is the badge in the table.
px.gloss.sees.dd: A building whose rent rises when you merely repaint the sign. While one chocolate shop (See's Candies) grew its profit 16-fold, it spent only $32 million on expansion — for an ordinary building that would have been a $400 million job. All the owner has to do is put up a new price tag.
px.gloss.title: Type glossary — how to read this table's ruler
px.gloss.toll.dd: A bridge everyone has to cross. The owner earns more whenever traffic grows, without building anything (ASML · Arm). The catch: there are very few such bridges in the world.
px.gloss.too_hard.dd: A building whose rent column 10 years out is blank. Not because it is a bad building, but because nobody can fill that column with confidence (in his 2000 letter Buffett said committing capital in such cases should be called speculation). Not a failing grade — the honesty of saying "we don't know."
px.gloss.uncovered.dd: A building the appraiser (our research) has not visited yet. Once forward EPS is filled in during earnings season, it gets a ruler.
px.notice_html: This is an observation experiment using Buffett's framework — not investment advice. The justified multiple (Justified MAX) is a subjective estimate, not a verified figure, and the gap is simply the arithmetic of plugging today's price into that estimate. Justified MAX is a ruler graded on forward earnings, so the zone calls and the counts below include only stocks measured on a forward basis — trailing (reported EPS) figures cannot be held against the same ruler and appear only as reference figures. The EPS estimate date is noted in the table. Nothing here is a buy or sell signal.
px.peak_tip: A warning light for cyclicals only. A P/E computed on peak earnings is a ceiling that looks like a floor — the moment Hynix looks "cheapest" at 4.8x may be the top of the cycle.
px.reason.float: stars whose appeal is the deposit, not the rent (float type)
px.reason.too_hard: stars whose rent 10 years out can't be written down (too hard)
px.reason.unlisted: stars with no market price at all (unlisted)
px.stripnote_html: Zone calls cover non-cyclical, forward-basis stocks only. Counted: {n} — the other {m} (trailing reference · cyclical) use a different ruler and get no zone.
